text:
nina (support): FYI BrightHealth reporting a surge of 504s and >300ms p95 starting ~01:12 UTC. They insist traffic should land in eu-central-1 but traces show hits to us-east-1. Trace id bh-77f2c. Billing alerts fired too. Can oncall triage?

sam (oncall): On it. Need the failing trace + client IP and which build they were on. Any recent network changes?

rachel (eng-sre): I grabbed the healthpulse logs and there's a routing reweight at 01:11:48 caused by eu-central-1 briefly showing "INCONSISTENT_TTL" from the aggregator. Snippet: 

```
2026-04-02T01:11:40Z hp-agg: recv probe eu-central-1 agent=agent-7 ttl=28
2026-04-02T01:11:46Z hp-agg: recv probe eu-central-1 agent=agent-7 ttl=2
2026-04-02T01:11:48Z hp-agg: state=DEGRADED region=eu-central-1 reason="ttl_variance"
2026-04-02T01:11:50Z hp-agg: route-adjust region=us-east-1 weight+=20%
```

That lines up with the customer's 504s. Suspect probe header mangling.

omar (network): We pushed a conn-compress change at 00:58 to reduce probe size for congested paths. If the compression step drops X-Health-TTL header sometimes, aggregator sees mixed TTLs.

sam (oncall): Repro request: can you give a minimal local repro so we can validate before hotfix?

rachel (eng-sre): Repro steps I used locally:
1) run probe agent with compression enabled: `./probe-agent --enable-compress`
2) emit two TTL batches to same agent: 
   - `for i in 1 2 3; do curl -H "X-Health-TTL: 28" http://localhost:9090/pulse; done`
   - `for i in 1 2; do curl -H "X-Health-TTL: 2" http://localhost:9090/pulse; done`
3) tail aggregator: `kubectl logs -l app=hp-agg --tail 200`
Observed: aggregator picks the low TTL entry and marks region DEGRADED, then triggers reweight.

nina (support): Sharing sanitized curl snippets with BrightHealth and letting them know we're investigating. They asked for ETA to avoid billing penalties.

sam (oncall): Short-term mitigations I'm rolling now: 1) disable conn compress for probe agents via config flag; 2) extend aggregator stability window from 20s to 60s; 3) pin BrightHealth's routing to eu-central-1 while we monitor. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: deploy release/2026-04-02-ttl-guard started by sam  rollout in eu-central-1, us-east-1, ap-south-1

omar (network): I'll open follow-up: ensure compression preserves X-Health-TTL or agents drop it consistently and emit default TTL. Ticket RED-4210.

rachel (eng-sre): Longer-term proposals: ignore TTL samples that differ >8s in same 45s window; require consensus from >=2 agents before marking DEGRADED; add hysteresis to route weight changes. I'll draft RED-4211 for aggregator consensus + canary plan.

sam (oncall): Monitoring: we're watching BrightHealth traces and healthpulse metrics. Initial metrics look stable, no further reweights in last 15m. I'll keep pin until end of 30m window.

nina (support): Customer update sent: they reported immediate drop in 504s after pin. I'll open the customer-facing postmortem and check billing offsets.

rachel (eng-sre): Verified in metrics: route weights steady and hp-agg TTL variance rate dropped to baseline. Marking this as resolved in channel; will post PR/links to RED-4211 and RED-4210 when available.

sam (oncall): Action items:
- RED-4210 (agent header/compression)  omar
- RED-4211 (aggregator consensus/hysteresis)  rachel
- Customer PM + billing review  nina

nina (support): Thanks everyone. Closing after final billing check. :thumbsup:
